C-SHARED-TERMINOLOGY.Summary: Reconcile the governing vocabulary with the owner's accepted industry-first naming rule and integrate the English shared terminology reference into the corpus and portal.

Goals.Goal: Permit established business and technology terms with accurate meanings, replacing blanket exclusions with distinctions between concepts.
Align English and Russian governing wording, record the owner's decision, and make the shared English reference reachable through the existing portal source path.

Constraints.Constraint: Authority: the owner selected common industry naming, explicitly included KPI, SLA, WIP, business case and value stream, and instructed “lets reconsile what we need to”. This approves reconciliation of the previously proposed rule and its directly affected corpus, translations and projections.

Preserve service commitments, measurement populations, cadence, authorities, identifiers and historical records. A familiar term does not establish an unrecorded SLA, KPI designation or methodology adoption.

The shared companion is English for this pass, as requested. Its Russian route uses the existing explicit source-language fallback; the governing amendments are paired in English and Russian. Neither language gains precedence.
Existing shared-reference edits are known input. Protect unrelated portal trials and immutable earlier approved plans.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Perform the later comprehensive Russian terminology rewrite, adopt every gray candidate, translate the entire new companion, commit, push, or deploy.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The governing vocabulary and Catalog no longer prohibit a common word merely because it belongs to an external framework; specific concepts remain distinct.
KPI, metric, SLA, WIP, WIP limit, business case and value stream have aligned definitions and appropriate relationships to AICC terms.
The recorded decision and language/source metadata accurately describe the reconciliation, and the English companion has a canonical portal page with working navigation and search.
Source validation, existing regression tests, scaffolding coverage and repeatable generated-site checks pass; representative pages are inspected in a browser.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Paired semantic review of terminology amendments and browser checks of both vocabulary pages, the new companion, language disclosure and navigation.
